page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the High Performance family. It features 2 shared vCPUs derived from a single physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 100 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2318.46 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1253.0. However, multi-core and memory performance are more limited. The stress-ng multi-core score is 4565.57, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 2253.0, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is measured at 180.62 GB/sec for cached reads and drops to 25.27 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. Database and web serving capabilities are also modest, with Redis SET operations reaching 2.1 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 2.03 GB/sec.

Due to its shared CPU allocation and lower multi-core performance, this server is positioned as a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require sustained, intensive compute resources. The inclusion of 100 GB of NVMe SSD storage provides fast local storage access, but the overall resource density makes it best suited for lightweight applications. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, development and testing environments, small-scale background tasks, and low-traffic applications where cost efficiency is prioritized over high-throughput multi-threaded execution.
